answer.rationale: The 18% mandate cannot be met through incumbent renegotiation (already refused, per c4 precedent). The low-cost vendor's quote meets the mandate directly. Verifying c2 confirms their onboarding speed and invoicing reliability under prior switching. However, at 94% assembly line utilization with zero buffer, switching the primary supply introduces delivery risk that a second source (c3 pattern) would mitigate but cannot be executed this cycle due to the one-decision constraint. Switching is the only path to meet the financial mandate while honoring the hard deadline. The decision flags downstream risk: if the low-cost vendor underperforms on reliability despite historical success, margin recovery becomes impossible mid-year. Preserving uncertainty means accepting the switch while recognizing the execution risk and maintaining readiness to activate a secondary source in the next review cycle if early performance signals warrant it.
